posts.title: How to Add an Animated Subscribe Button to Your Video
posts.description: Add an animated subscribe, like or bell button with a transparent background — and a click-and-bell sound — to your video in a free browser editor.
posts.excerpt: Add an animated subscribe, like or bell button with a transparent background — and a click-and-bell sound — to your video in a free browser editor.
posts.imageAlt: How to Add an Animated Subscribe Button to Your Video
posts.html:
A short "subscribe" reminder near the start or end of a video is a simple way to grow a channel. Reelsmith includes animated buttons that are ready to use, with transparent backgrounds — no green screen or background removal needed.

1. Open the Library

Click the Library tab (next to Project, Effects and Captions). You'll find:

  • Subscribe Button, Like Button, Comment Button and Notification Bell
  • Like · Comment · Subscribe (all three in one)
  • Follow Button, Share Button, Click Cursor, Bouncing Arrow and Progress Bar

Hover over a card to preview the animation.

2. Add it to the video

  • Double-click a card to add it at the playhead, or
  • drag it onto a track above your video.

It's placed on V2 or higher, sized for your frame — including vertical 9:16 videos.

3. Make it yours

Select the graphic and open Effect Controls ▸ Graphic to change the text (for example SUBSCRIBE → JOIN) and the colours. Move and resize it in the Program monitor, and drag the clip's edges on the timeline to make it stay longer or shorter.

You can also add an In, Out or Loop animation from Effects ▸ Animations — try Pop in and Pulse as a loop.

The click-and-bell sound

The Subscribe Button comes with a matching sound: a click as the cursor presses the button, then a bell as the bell icon swings. The sound is placed on an audio track and linked to the graphic, so they move together.

Don't want the sound? Select the graphic, press ⌘L (Ctrl+L on Windows) to unlink it, then click the audio clip and press Delete.

When to show it

  • After you've delivered something useful — viewers are more likely to subscribe once they've got value.
  • For 3–5 seconds, in a corner that doesn't cover faces or important text.
  • Once or twice per video, not constantly.
Tip: Have your own button animation on a white or green background? See How to remove the background from a video.

posts.title: How to Add Subtitles to a Video Automatically (Free, Online)
posts.description: Generate captions from speech in your browser, edit them, and burn them into your video or export an .srt file — free and without uploading your video.
posts.excerpt: Generate captions from speech in your browser, edit them, and burn them into your video or export an .srt file — free and without uploading your video.
posts.imageAlt: How to Add Subtitles to a Video Automatically (Free, Online)
posts.html:
Captions make your videos easier to follow with the sound off, help viewers who are deaf or hard of hearing, and keep people watching longer. Reelsmith can write them for you from the speech in your video. The speech recognition runs on your own computer, so the audio is never uploaded.

What you need

  • A video with clear speech (or a separate voice-over track).
  • A recent version of Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox. Chrome and Edge are the fastest because they can use your graphics chip.

1. Put the video on the timeline

Open the editor, click New Project (or Start Editing) and drag your video onto the timeline. If the audio is on its own track, that works too — captions are made from everything you can hear.

2. Generate the captions

  1. Open the Captions tab in the bottom-left panel and click Auto-generate. You can also use Captions ▸ Auto-generate Captions… in the menu bar.
  2. Choose what to transcribe: the Entire sequence, just the part between your In and Out points, or the selected clips.
  3. Pick the spoken language, or leave Detect automatically.
  4. Choose the accuracy. Base is a good balance; Tiny is fastest; Small is the most accurate for difficult audio and less common languages.
  5. Click Generate.

The first time, the caption engine downloads once (about 45–95 MB, depending on the model) and stays in your browser. After that it starts almost instantly.

Tip: Tick Translate the captions into English to get English subtitles from speech in another language.

3. Check and fix the words

Speech recognition is good but not perfect — names, brands and technical words often need a correction.

  • Click a caption in the Captions panel and edit its text.
  • Drag caption clips on the CC track to move them, or drag their edges to change how long they stay on screen.
  • Click Add at playhead to add a caption by hand.

4. Style them

Click Style… in the Captions panel to change the text size, colour, background box, position and margin so the subtitles fit your video.

5. Export with captions

Click Export. Under Captions choose:

  • Burn into the video — the subtitles become part of the picture (best for Instagram, TikTok and Shorts).
  • Save as an .srt file only — upload it as a subtitle track on YouTube or Vimeo, where viewers can turn it on and off.
  • Burn in and save an .srt file — both.

You can also use Captions ▸ Export Captions (.srt)… at any time.

Hide captions without deleting them

Untick Show captions in the Captions panel (or click CC in the Program monitor). Hidden captions are left out of exports unless you choose Burn into the video.

Free up the space later

The caption engine stays in your browser for next time. To remove it, choose Captions ▸ Remove Caption Engine… — it downloads again whenever you need it.

Read the full reference in Captions and subtitles.

posts.title: How to Make Animated Text and 3D Titles
posts.description: Create eye-catching titles in a free online video editor — 3D, gradient and two-tone text, word-by-word animation, and ready-made title templates.
posts.excerpt: Create eye-catching titles in a free online video editor — 3D, gradient and two-tone text, word-by-word animation, and ready-made title templates.
posts.imageAlt: How to Make Animated Text and 3D Titles
posts.html:
A good title grabs attention in the first second. Reelsmith gives you three ways to make one: start from a template, apply a one-click style, or build your own look with text effects and animations.

The fastest way: a title template

Open Effects ▸ Title Templates and double-click one — for example Retro Pop 3D Title, Epic 3D Title, Kinetic Words or Bouncy Words. It's added at the playhead, sized for your frame. Double-click the text in the Program monitor to type your own words.

Type your own title

  1. Press T for the Type tool.
  2. Click in the Program monitor and type. Press ⌘Enter (Ctrl+Enter on Windows) or click outside to finish.
  3. Drag the text to move it; drag the corner handles to resize.
  4. Set the font, size, colour, outline, shadow and background box in Effect Controls ▸ Text.

One-click styles

With the title selected, double-click a style in Effects ▸ Text Styles: Retro Pop 3D, Epic Gold 3D, Gradient Bold, Two-Tone, Sticker Outline, Candy 3D, Gold Luxe, Comic Burst 3D, Neon, Elegant and more. Applying a new style replaces the old one, so you can try several quickly.

Build your own look

Effect Controls ▸ Text Effects has:

  • Gradient fill with two colours and an angle.
  • 3D extrude with depth, direction and side colour.
  • Highlight words: wrap a word in asterisks — Make it *pop* — and it takes the highlight colour.
  • Halftone dots, outer outline, offset shadow, glow and letter spacing.

Animate it

Drag an animation from Effects ▸ Animations onto the title:

  • In: Pop, Zoom, Slide, Fade Up, Blur In, Bounce, Stamp, Typewriter, and text-only Words Pop, Words Rise, Letters Drop and more.
  • Out: the same moves in reverse, plus Erase.
  • Loop: Pulse, Float, Wobble, Letter Wave or Word Bounce while the title is on screen.

Each title has one In, one Out and one Loop animation. Set their duration, speed and strength in Effect Controls ▸ Animation.

Tips for titles that read well

  • Keep it short — three to six words.
  • Use strong contrast: a light fill with a dark outline or shadow is readable on any background.
  • Leave a little space at the edges; click Safe in the Program monitor to see the safe zone.

More detail: Titles and 3D, gradient, halftone and animated text.

posts.title: 7 Editing Tips That Make Short Videos Easier to Watch
posts.description: Practical, beginner-friendly editing tips for Shorts, Reels and TikTok — hooks, pacing, captions, sound and framing — with how to do each in Reelsmith.
posts.excerpt: Practical, beginner-friendly editing tips for Shorts, Reels and TikTok — hooks, pacing, captions, sound and framing — with how to do each in Reelsmith.
posts.html:
Short videos live or die in the first few seconds. These seven habits make a noticeable difference, and each one takes less than a minute in Reelsmith.

1. Start with the most interesting moment

Don't warm up. Open on the result, the punchline or the question your video answers. Drag your best clip to the start of the timeline, or trim the slow opening with the razor tool (C).

2. Cut every pause

Silences that feel natural in conversation feel slow on screen. Play through, split at the start and end of each pause, and delete the gap. The waveform on audio clips shows you where the pauses are. See Deleting clips and closing gaps.

3. Add captions

Many people watch with the sound off. Generate captions automatically, correct any wrong words, and choose Burn into the video when you export.

4. Put a headline on screen

A few bold words in the first second tell viewers why they should stay. Press T, type, and apply a style from Effects ▸ Text Styles. A Words Pop animation draws the eye without being distracting. More in How to make animated text and 3D titles.

5. Change the picture every few seconds

Cut to a different angle, zoom in on the action, or add a quick transition such as Whip Pan or Zoom In. Even on a single shot, slowly keyframing Scale from 100 % to 110 % adds energy. See Effect Controls and keyframes.

6. Make the sound clean and consistent

Viewers forgive average video, but not bad audio. Use Clip ▸ Normalize Loudness… so every clip is equally loud, and Effects ▸ Smart Audio ▸ Auto Duck Music Under Voice so music never drowns out speech. Our audio tutorial covers the rest.

7. Frame for vertical screens

Keep faces and text in the middle third of a 9:16 frame, where app buttons and captions won't cover them. Click Safe in the Program monitor to see the margins. The vertical video tutorial shows how to reframe landscape footage.

Put these together and even a simple phone clip feels intentional. Open the editor and try them on your next video.

posts.title: Introducing Reelsmith, a Free Video Editor That Runs in Your Browser
posts.description: Reelsmith brings a real multi-track editor — timeline, titles, transitions, color, audio and auto captions — to the browser, with no upload and no sign-up.
posts.excerpt: Reelsmith brings a real multi-track editor — timeline, titles, transitions, color, audio and auto captions — to the browser, with no upload and no sign-up.
posts.imageAlt: Introducing Reelsmith, a Free Video Editor That Runs in Your Browser
posts.html:
Most online video editors fall into one of two camps. Some are template apps: quick, but you can't really edit. Others upload your footage to a server, make you wait, and add a watermark unless you pay.

Reelsmith takes a different approach. It is a full non-linear editor — the kind of tool editors use every day — that runs entirely in your browser, on your own computer.

What you get

  • A proper timeline with unlimited tracks, ripple and rolling edits, slip and slide, the razor tool and frame-accurate trimming.
  • Titles that look designed: 3D, gradient and two-tone styles, plus word-by-word and letter-by-letter animations.
  • 30 transitions, from a classic cross dissolve to whip pans, glitches and colourful shape wipes.
  • Color grading with curves, color wheels and scopes.
  • Audio tools: normalization, EQ, compression, noise gate, voice effects, sound effects and automatic music ducking.
  • Auto captions in more than 20 languages, generated on your device.
  • Fast export to MP4 or WebM, with presets for YouTube, Shorts, Reels, TikTok and Instagram.

Nothing to upload

When you import a video into Reelsmith, it stays where it is on your disk. Your browser reads it, shows it on the timeline and, when you export, writes a new file back to your computer. There is no upload queue, no file-size limit set by a server, and no copy of your footage anywhere else. We explain how this works in Why your videos never leave your computer.

Free, without the catch

There is no account to create and no watermark on your exports. Open reelsmithapp.com and start editing.

Where to start

  • New to editing? Follow Your first edit in 5 minutes.
  • Making short-form videos? Read How to make vertical videos for Shorts, Reels and TikTok.
  • Want subtitles? See How to add subtitles to a video automatically.

Reelsmith is new, and it gets better with your feedback. If something doesn't work the way you expect, or you'd like a feature, tell us with Report a bug or Request a feature.

posts.title: How to Make Quiet Video Audio Louder (and Clearer)
posts.description: Boost low volume in a video, even out loud and quiet parts, remove background noise and separate the audio from the picture — free in your browser.
posts.excerpt: Boost low volume in a video, even out loud and quiet parts, remove background noise and separate the audio from the picture — free in your browser.
posts.html:
A great shot with sound you can barely hear is a common problem with phone and camera footage. Here is how to fix it in Reelsmith, from the quickest fix to a polished result.

Quick fix: raise the volume

  1. Click the clip on the timeline.
  2. In Effect Controls ▸ Audio, raise Volume. 100 % is the original level; you can go up to 300 %.
  3. Play it back and watch the meters on the right of the timeline. Keep the peaks below 0 dB — if the top of the meter turns red, the sound is close to distorting.

Prefer exact numbers? Select the clip and press G for Audio Gain… to add or remove decibels.

Better: normalize the loudness

Different clips are often recorded at different levels. Select them and choose Clip ▸ Normalize Loudness…, then pick a target. Every clip is brought to the same perceived loudness, so viewers don't have to keep reaching for the volume.

Even out loud and quiet parts

If some words are loud and others quiet, drag Effects ▸ Audio Effects ▸ Compressor onto the clip. It turns down the loudest moments so you can raise the overall level without distortion. Use Make-up gain to bring it back up.

Clean up the sound

Also in Effects ▸ Audio Effects:

  • High-Pass removes rumble from traffic, wind and handling noise (80 Hz is a good start for voices).
  • DeHum removes the 50 or 60 Hz buzz from electrical equipment.
  • Noise Gate silences the hiss between words.
  • Parametric EQ — lift the highs a little for clearer speech, or cut the lows to reduce boominess.

Work on the audio separately

Video and audio from the same file are linked, so they move together. To edit the sound on its own — for example to boost it, move it, or delete it — select the clip and press ⌘L (Ctrl+L on Windows), or right-click ▸ Unlink. You don't need to unlink just to change the volume, though: selecting the clip is enough.

Tip: Recording a narration? Click the mic button on an audio track to record a voice-over straight into the timeline.

Music under speech

Put background music on its own track, select it and apply Effects ▸ Smart Audio ▸ Auto Duck Music Under Voice. The music dips automatically whenever someone speaks.

More detail: Working with audio, Audio effects and Detaching audio from video.

posts.title: Why Your Videos Never Leave Your Computer
posts.description: How Reelsmith edits, captions and exports video entirely inside your browser — and why that is faster and more private than uploading.
posts.excerpt: How Reelsmith edits, captions and exports video entirely inside your browser — and why that is faster and more private than uploading.
posts.html:
"Online video editor" usually means "upload your video to someone else's computer". Reelsmith works differently: it is a website, but the editing happens on your machine. Here's how, and why it matters.

The browser has become a video workstation

Modern browsers ship with the building blocks of a video editor:

  • Hardware video decoding and encoding (WebCodecs) — the same video chips your computer uses to play and record video.
  • The graphics chip (WebGL and WebGPU) for real-time effects, color correction and compositing.
  • A professional audio engine (Web Audio) for mixing, EQ, compression and effects.
  • Direct file access — in Chrome and Edge, a website can read the files you choose and save a new file where you say, with your permission.

Reelsmith uses these directly. When you press play, your browser decodes the frames, Reelsmith composites titles, effects and transitions on the graphics chip, and the result appears in the Program monitor. When you export, the same pipeline runs faster than real time and the encoder writes an MP4 straight to your disk.

What this means for you

  • Privacy. Client footage, family videos and unreleased work are never copied to a server.
  • No waiting for uploads. A 4 GB file is ready to edit the moment you import it.
  • No server-side limits. File size and length are limited only by your computer.
  • It keeps working when the connection drops. Once the page has loaded, editing doesn't need the internet.

What about auto captions?

Speech recognition usually happens in the cloud. In Reelsmith it doesn't. The first time you click Generate, your browser downloads an open-source speech model (Whisper) once and keeps it. From then on, your audio is transcribed on your device — it is never sent anywhere. You can remove the model at any time from Captions ▸ Remove Caption Engine.

What is stored, and where

  • Projects you save are kept in your browser's storage on your computer. Use File ▸ Download Project File for a backup you can move to another machine.
  • Your media stays in its original folder. In Chrome and Edge, Reelsmith remembers which files a project uses, so it can reopen them next time after you click Reconnect files.

The full details are in our Privacy Policy.

The trade-offs

Doing everything locally means your computer does the work. A recent laptop handles 1080p editing comfortably; very long 4K projects are smoother on a desktop with plenty of memory. Chrome and Edge currently offer the best performance and file access; Safari and Firefox work, with exports saved to Downloads.

Ready to try it? Open the editor — there is nothing to install.

posts.title: How to Remove the Background from a Video or Logo
posts.description: Make a white, black or green background transparent — for logos, subscribe animations and green-screen clips — in a free browser video editor.
posts.excerpt: Make a white, black or green background transparent — for logos, subscribe animations and green-screen clips — in a free browser video editor.
posts.imageAlt: How to Remove the Background from a Video or Logo
posts.html:
Overlay graphics are everywhere: a subscribe animation in the corner, a logo watermark, a green-screen clip of you over a new background. They usually come with a solid background that has to go. Reelsmith removes it by colour in a couple of clicks.

Remove a video background

This works for animations on a white, black or green background, such as a like-and-subscribe clip.

  1. Put your main video on V1.
  2. Put the overlay video on V2, directly above it.
  3. Right-click the overlay clip ▸ Remove Background. (Or select it and click Remove Background in Effect Controls.)

Reelsmith looks at the edges of the frame, detects the background colour and sets up the Ultra Key effect for you.

Fine-tune it

In Effect Controls ▸ Ultra Key:

  • Mode: Brightness for white, black or grey backgrounds; Colour for green or blue screens.
  • Keep inside (edges only): removes only the background that touches the edges of the frame, so white text or icons inside the animation stay visible.
  • Tolerance: raise it if a light fringe remains; lower it if parts of the animation disappear.
  • Softness: smooths the edge.

Place and size it

Use Effect Controls ▸ Motion — or drag the clip in the Program monitor — to scale it down and move it, for example to the bottom of the frame.

Remove a logo or image background

  1. Import the logo.
  2. Right-click it in the Project panel (or on the timeline) ▸ Remove Background…
  3. The preview shows transparent areas as a checkerboard. Click the preview to pick the background colour, or Shift+click to add more colours for gradients.
  4. Choose Background touching the edges to keep white parts inside the logo, or This colour everywhere to also clear the holes in letters like O, A and e.
  5. Adjust Tolerance and Edge softness, tick Trim transparent edges if you like, and click Remove Background.

A new transparent PNG is added to the Project panel and your clip switches to it. The original stays untouched.

When colour removal isn't enough

Background removal works by colour, so it's best for graphics and screens with a plain background. To cut out a person in an everyday photo or video, draw a mask around them and use mask tracking to follow the movement.

Tip: Need a subscribe button and don't have one? The Library tab has animated buttons with transparent backgrounds already — see Add an animated subscribe button.

posts.title: How to Make Vertical Videos for Shorts, Reels and TikTok
posts.description: Edit 9:16 vertical videos in your browser — turn landscape footage vertical, add captions and text, and export at the right size for Shorts, Reels and TikTok.
posts.excerpt: Edit 9:16 vertical videos in your browser — turn landscape footage vertical, add captions and text, and export at the right size for Shorts, Reels and TikTok.
posts.imageAlt: How to Make Vertical Videos for Shorts, Reels and TikTok
posts.html:
Short-form platforms expect vertical 9:16 video at 1080×1920. Here is how to set that up in Reelsmith, whether you filmed vertically or horizontally.

If you filmed vertically

Start a project and drop in your phone clip. In a new sequence, the first video you add sets the frame size — a vertical clip makes a 9:16 sequence automatically. A message confirms it, and ⌘Z (Ctrl+Z on Windows) undoes it.

If you filmed horizontally

  1. Choose Sequence ▸ Sequence Settings… and pick the Vertical 9:16 (1080×1920) preset.
  2. Add your landscape clip. It sits in the middle with empty space above and below.
  3. Select the clip and open Effect Controls ▸ Motion. Raise Scale until the picture fills the height, then drag it left or right in the Program monitor to frame your subject.
Tip: If your subject moves around, add Position keyframes so the frame follows them. See Effect Controls and keyframes.

Make it work without sound

Most people scroll with the sound off, so text matters:

  • Auto captions: Captions ▸ Auto-generate Captions… writes subtitles from your speech — see How to add subtitles automatically.
  • A hook in the first second: press T, click the video and type a short headline. Then try a style from Effects ▸ Text Styles and an animation such as Words Pop from Effects ▸ Animations — In.
  • Keep text in the middle: the top and bottom of the screen are often covered by the app's buttons and captions. Click Safe in the Program monitor to show safe margins.

Keep it moving

  • Cut out pauses with the razor tool (C), then delete the gaps (see Deleting clips and closing gaps) so the video never stalls.
  • Use quick transitions like Whip Pan, Zoom In or Flash between scenes, and the Zoom Punch (beat) effect from Effects ▸ Creative Effects for emphasis.
  • Add a sound effect (Effects ▸ Sound Effects) on key moments.

Export at the right size

Click Export and choose the YouTube Shorts / Reels / TikTok (9:16) preset — 1080×1920 H.264 MP4. If your sequence is already vertical, Match Source gives the same result. Then upload the file from your phone or computer.
